texts.preamble: Rajeev Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 November, 2019 Author: Vishal Mishra Bench: Vishal Mishra The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-46606-2019 (Rajeev Kumar Gupta Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) Gwalior, Dated :21/11/2019 Shri V.K. Agarwal, learned counsel for the applicant. Shri Sanjay Bahirani, Public Prosecutor for the respondent- State.
texts.facts: The applicant has filed this first application u/S.439, Cr.P.C. for grant of bail. The applicant has been arrested by Police Station Special Task Force Bhopal, Unit Gwalior (M.P.), in connection with Crime No.12/2019 registered in relation to the offence punishable u/Ss.420, 272, 273, 120-B of IPC and u/S.51 and 59 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter. He has not committed the offence in any manner. The applicant is in custody since 9.9.2019. It is alleged by the counsel for the applicant that in identical circumstances this Hon'ble Court vide its order dated 22.10.2019 passed in M.Cr.C. No.43734/2019 (Rajendra Prasad Gupta Vs. State of M.P.) has allowed the bail application of other co-accused, therefore, he claims parity with the other co-accused person and prays for grant of bail. THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH MCRC-46606-2019 (RAJEEV KUMAR GUPTA Vs THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH) Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State has opposed the bail application and contended that the case of present applicant is not identical with the Rajendra Prasad Gupta and has contended that there is specific recovery from the possession of present applicant and articles are being found adulterated in the FSL report. He fairly submits that there is no criminal antecedents against the present applicant. He admits that investigation in the matter is over and charge-sheet has been filed on 27.9.2019 but he prays for dismissal of the bail application.
